info.description: Recruiting platform API: job requisitions, candidates, application pipelines, and ML-scored candidate shortlists.

get.description:
Report service health, including a real round-trip to PostgreSQL.

Returns 503 when the database is unreachable so an orchestrator can pull
the instance out of rotation rather than serving requests that will fail.

put.summary: Upload a resume file, replacing the stored text
put.description:
Ingest a PDF or plain-text resume into ``resume_text``.

PUT rather than POST: the stored text is replaced wholesale, so re-uploading
the same file twice leaves the candidate in the same state.

post.summary: Apply a candidate to a job
post.description:
Open an application at the first pipeline stage.

A missing job or candidate is a 404 naming which one; an unopen requisition
or a repeat application is a 409, since both conflict with existing state
rather than being malformed requests. A job or candidate deleted while the
request runs is refused by its foreign key and gets the same 404.

patch.summary: Update an application, including its pipeline stage
patch.description:
Partially update an application.

A status change must be a legal move through the pipeline; an illegal one
is a 409 naming the stages that *are* reachable. Re-sending the current
status is a no-op, so a retried request does not fail.

delete.description:
Hard-delete an application.

Withdrawing a candidate is a status change; this is for removing a record
created in error, which is why it leaves no pipeline history behind.

get.summary: Full pipeline history for one application
get.description:
Every status move this application has made, oldest first.

Answers "how long did screening take" and similar questions without
reconstructing history from ``updated_at``. A handful of rows per
application, so this returns the whole list rather than a page.

schema.title: Response List Stage Events Api V1 Applications  Application Id  Stage Events Get

post.summary: Reopen a rejected or withdrawn application
post.description:
Put a rejected or withdrawn application back at the start of the pipeline.

Deliberately separate from a status PATCH, which still cannot move a
finished application. The stage event records the real ``from_status``, so
the rejected or withdrawn stint keeps its duration. The same row is reopened
rather than a new one created, since a candidate holds one application per
job; and like applying in the first place, it needs the requisition open.

post.summary: Score a candidate pool against a job and cache the ranking
post.description:
Score candidates against a job with the trained matcher, rank them and cache the scores.

Leaving out ``candidate_ids`` scores every candidate on file. The whole
pool is scored and cached in ``match_scores``; ``limit`` only trims what
comes back, and ranks are positions within this pool. Scoring again with
an unchanged matcher updates the cached rows rather than adding more.

A missing job or candidate is a 404, checked before the matcher is
loaded. A missing or unreadable matcher is a 503 naming the command that
regenerates it (see ``app.main``).

A candidate deleted mid-run, before the run wrote its score, fails the
write. The run is then rolled back, re-read and scored again, and the
candidate has dropped out of the pool (or is now a 404, if it was asked for
by id). A row someone else inserted first is updated in place. Up to three
attempts are made, and only a third failure is answered with a 409.

Other runs of the same job, an edit of the job and a delete of it take
turns with this run's write (see :func:`score_pool`). A run that waited on
another updates the rows that one saved instead of racing it to insert
them, and a delete already under way finishes first, making this a 404.

get.summary: A job's cached ranking under the current matcher
get.description:
Page through the scores cached for a job, best first. Nothing is scored here.

Only scores from the matcher currently on disk are listed; rows an
earlier model left behind stay in the table but are never mixed in. Ranks
run across everything cached for the job under that matcher, so they stay
1 to ``total`` even when some candidates were scored in a separate,
smaller run -- which is the one case where they differ from the rank that
run returned. A score is as of its ``scored_at``: editing the job or a
candidate afterwards does not rescore it.

The matcher is loaded here too, not just hashed, so a file that exists
but cannot be used is the same 503 scoring gives. Hashing alone would
list nothing for it -- no score can carry the version of a file that
never loaded -- and every shortlist would look emptied.

get.summary: A job's ranked shortlist as a PDF
get.description:
The best ``limit`` candidates cached for the job under the current matcher.

Nothing is scored here: the ranks, scores and features are the ones
``GET /jobs/{id}/matches`` lists. A job with nothing cached under the
current matcher is a 409 pointing at the scoring endpoint, rather than an
empty report that reads as if nobody fitted.

get.summary: One candidate's scorecard for a job as a PDF
get.description:
The candidate's cached score for the job, its rank, skills, profile and features.

The rank is the candidate's position in the job's cached ranking, the same
one ``GET /jobs/{id}/matches`` gives it: best score first, ties to the lower
candidate id. A missing job or candidate is a 404; a candidate with no
score for the job under the current matcher is a 409.

required_skill_coverage.title: Required Skill Coverage
required_skill_coverage.description: Share of the job's required skills the candidate lists; 1.0 if the job requires none

preferred_skill_coverage.title: Preferred Skill Coverage
preferred_skill_coverage.description: Share of the job's preferred skills the candidate lists; 1.0 if the job prefers none

skill_jaccard.title: Skill Jaccard
skill_jaccard.description: Overlap between the job's skills, required and preferred, and the candidate's, over their union; 0.0 when both are empty

experience_gap.title: Experience Gap
experience_gap.description: Years short of the job's minimum, divided by 5, capped at 1.0

experience_surplus.title: Experience Surplus
experience_surplus.description: Years beyond the job's minimum, divided by 5, capped at 1.0

seniority_distance.title: Seniority Distance
seniority_distance.description: Seniority levels between candidate and job, either direction, as a share of the widest possible gap

seniority_direction.title: Seniority Direction
seniority_direction.description: seniority_distance with a sign: negative under-levelled, positive over

education_fit.title: Education Fit
education_fit.description: 1.0 when the candidate meets or exceeds the education required, down to 0.0

MatchFeatures.title: MatchFeatures
MatchFeatures.description:
The engineered features behind a score, as ``match_scores.features`` stores them.

Exactly :data:`app.ml.features.FEATURE_NAMES`, in that order. The TF-IDF
half of the matcher's input is not broken out per score: the calibrated
matcher keeps one fitted vocabulary per calibration fold, so there is no
single text similarity to report back.
